parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation since 2008, and a health-resolution covering gender identity in care access are positives. But the operative regime shows state police and parapolice as documented aggressors against LGBTI people inside a broader impunity climate, attacks 'generally culturally accepted and legally unenforced', underreporting from fear, and suppressed media — thin or no recourse (tier 3 with a documented state-hand component, tier 2). No visitor-facing border, document, facility or custody exposures are documented, but the thin dossier cannot show their absence; extrapolating from weak rule of law and documented police participation in violence, the traveller who is outed faces meaningful assault/extortion risk with little remedy, not custodial catastrophe. This sits below jurisdictions with working remedies (0.55–0.65) and above those with enforced criminalisation or sweeps (0.15–0.25).

entry_documents.protection: No visitor-facing border or marker restriction is recorded; decriminalisation since 2008 removes latent status law.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented document-checkout pathway; unknown whether mismatched documents trigger questioning.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State police named among aggressors against LGBTI people (10 documented in 2021; tied with family members 2022); detention conditions not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police aggression inside an impunity climate converts any police contact into outing/harm exposure.

federal_state_facilities.protection: 2014 health resolution bars discrimination in public and private health units on gender identity and expression — covers facilities-linked care.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Resolution's enforcement for foreign visitors is not documented.

care_services.protection: Health ministry resolution (2014) prohibits gender-identity/expression discrimination in all health units — a resident-facing but trans-specific standard.
care_services.interaction: General impunity climate and weak reporting channels may blunt the resolution in practice.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Foreign-government 2023 report lists violence/threats against LGBTI persons as significant violations amid a police/parapolice harassment campaign authorities did not investigate; violence 'generally culturally accepted and legally unenforced'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2011 UN joint statement support is rhetorical only.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State non-investigation signals state tolerance of anti-trans abuse.

minors_guardians.interaction: No youth-specific care-access or family-travel findings recorded; the trans adult with a minor faces the same undocumented landscape as the solo adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented annual counts (35–67 assaults/yr 2021–2023, hate crimes, murders, extortion 2023), undercounted per sources; trans women most targeted; police among aggressors; underreporting from fear and poor legal outcomes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw counts without denominator cannot be rate-compared; media suppression since 2018 limits visibility of the true pattern.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Attacks largely unreported for fear of retaliation and dismal legal results; no trans-specific hate-crime aggravator documented; sexual-orientation aggravator may not cover gender identity.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Article 315 employment provision and Article 36(5) aggravator are resident-facing; 2014 health resolution is the only trans-inclusive standard.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknown: family-code challenge outcome, regional-court opinion implementation, custody practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia shows organised police targeting of trans visitors with near-universal stops. Here police aggression against LGBTI people is documented but not shown as a visitor-directed stop regime; severity of routine contact is lower, so the case sits above 0.35.

Ostrovia's sporadic transit-police harassment with stalling complaints parallels this dossier's police-as-aggressor pattern, but Ostrovia has functioning ombudsman routes and no impunity regime; this jurisdiction's documented non-investigation and suppressed media push it below 0.55.

Alderland has similar late-night assault risk but working prosecutions, police review, and protective orders. This jurisdiction's impunity climate and unenforced law against anti-LGBTI violence place it well below 0.75.

Meridia's police extortion with dismissed complaints resembles the documented police aggression plus impunity here. This dossier lacks an enforced criminal statute and shows some formal protections, so it sits somewhat above 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime pairs decriminalisation and a trans-inclusive health non-discrimination resolution with a documented pattern of anti-LGBTI violence in which state police participate and authorities do not investigate. No visitor-specific border, facility or custody exposure is documented, but the thin record cannot confirm their absence, and the governing extrapolation — weak rule of law, impunity, suppressed media, underreported attacks — resolves uncertainty downward, not to neutral. The operative risk for an outed visitor is societal or police violence, extortion and service friction with negligible recourse; not imprisonment. That places the jurisdiction in the Elevated band's upper range, similar to a friction-plus-impunity regime, above criminalising states and below remedy-bearing ones.
